The test image shows a tomato stem cut longitudinally at the soil line, with white fungal material visible on the stem exterior and interior, collapsed brown leaves, and sandy soil. This points toward a soil-line stem disease. Top candidates: **Southern_Blight**, **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**, **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**, **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**.

Now I'll check one reference from each candidate class.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Stem split longitudinally at the soil line revealing pale/cream interior, white fungal material visible on the stem exterior near the soil, plant collapsed with dead brown leaves, sandy soil background.
- **Southern_Blight** (stem ref 1575059): Stem cut open showing pale bleached interior with browning margins — very close match to test image.
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (stem ref 5593844): White bleached stem with dark black sclerotia (rice-grain-sized) embedded in stem — black sclerotia not clearly visible in test image.
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt** (stem ref 1568041): Brown vascular discoloration throughout interior — does not match the white appearance in test image.
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers** (stem ref 5530065): Dark brown/black canker at soil line, no white mycelium — does not match test image.

**Decision**: The white fungal material at the stem base near soil line, the bleached/pale stem tissue, and plant collapse best match **Southern_Blight**. Sclerotinia is ruled out by absence of visible hard black sclerotia. Southern Bacterial Wilt doesn't produce white fungal growth. Alternaria shows dark cankers, not white mycelium.
